name: Treetops Lodge & Estate
positioning: A private wilderness lodge and estate of native forest, waterfalls, lakes and trout streams 20 minutes from Rotorua, reserved exclusively for guests
best_for: Travelers who want hiking, fly fishing and wildlife on a private estate
Couples and families looking for secluded villas with fireplaces

facts.text: Treetops Lodge & Estate is located 20 minutes from Rotorua, in secluded countryside in New Zealand's central North Island.
The estate is reserved exclusively for guests.
In 1986, founder John Sax began acquiring land near Rotorua and restoring it by replanting native trees, establishing wetlands and protecting wildlife habitats.
The villas are built with native timber felled and milled on-site.
Valley Villas have French doors opening to a private patio facing the Horo Bluffs.
The estate's luxury tents have premium king bedding, timber furnishings, a private ensuite and outdoor living spaces overlooking native forest.
The spa offers private jacuzzis and massage therapy beneath native trees.
Guests can kayak on the estate's Lake Reflection.
Heli fishing gives access to wilderness terrain not easily reached by other means.
A guided private estate tour offers chances to view and photograph stag, water buffalo, sheep, goats and birdlife.
Dishes are created from organic ingredients grown on the estate.
Conservation programmes include reforestation, wildlife population management, invasive species control and collaboration with local environmental organisations.

highlights.text: The estate features four waterfalls and lakes, seven trout streams and over 70 km (35 miles) of private hiking and adventure trails.
A guided walk through fern forest leads to Bridal Veil Falls, the lodge's own private waterfall.
Each villa has a private terrace, a fireplace and direct access to trails, lakes and streams.
Glow worm caverns are a few minutes from the main lodge.
Treetops Spa treatments use estate-reared, 100% raw Manuka honey.

considerations.text: Weather in the Horohoro and greater Rotorua area can vary, and all activities are subject to suitable weather conditions.
The lodge suggests a stay of three to four nights to enjoy the estate at a relaxed pace.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
